units.source_text: 在箱根的旅馆里，名人、大竹七段还有我曾打过几次台球，名人巧取七十。

en.t: At the inn in Hakone, the Master, Otake 7-dan, and I played billiards several times, and the Master deftly scored seventy.

units.source_text: 大竹七段像下围棋似的详细说了取得的分数：“我四十二，吴清源十四……”

en.t: Otake 7-dan described the scores in detail, as though he were playing go: “I had forty-two, Wu Qingyuan fourteen...”

units.source_text: 名人每击一球，不仅充分思考，连架势也都摆好，然后才挥杆一击。

en.t: Each time the Master struck a ball, he not only thought it through fully but even set his stance carefully before finally swinging the cue.

units.source_text: 他击球的次数很多，都是经过长时间周密思考的。

en.t: He took many shots, and every one of them came after long and meticulous consideration.

units.source_text: 一般想来，打台球也会因球和人体之间的运动速度，产生打得顺手的情况，但在名人身上没有这种运动系统。

en.t: Ordinarily, one would think that in billiards too, the speed of movement between the balls and the human body creates moments when the shot comes easily, but in the Master there was no such system of motion.

units.source_text: 看着名人挥杆击球的一刹那，真叫人着急。

en.t: Watching the instant when the Master swung the cue and struck the ball was truly exasperating.

units.source_text: 继续看下去，我感到名人有一股哀伤而又亲切的气质。

en.t: As I kept watching, I felt that the Master had an air that was both sorrowful and warmly familiar.
